output.answer: E8.1 (funding cash-and-carry: long spot + short perp, delta-neutral) was closed on 7 Sep 2026 because it failed its profitability test on all 8 funding series tested (Binance ETH/BTC 2019–2026, Hyperliquid ETH/BTC 900d, windows 30d/90d): 8/8 series showed no edge versus the USDC-lending benchmark (Aave/Morpho BENCH_APR 3.8%/yr). Annualized funding was 10.8–13.9%/yr, but after costs (0.25%/window round trip, 50% of capital idle as margin, and the USDC benchmark) the breakeven funding threshold was 9.6–13.7%/yr, so only 17–56% of windows had positive edge, the last-180-day windows were negative everywhere, and 2022 (the bear market) had 0% winning windows. It only worked in 2020–21. The class was closed with no new data to return; a conditional exception was noted only if funding exceeded 20%/yr sustained for weeks (a signal, not a strategy).

output.answer: E8.4 (Aerodrome cbBTC/WETH, wide ±40% position) was closed on 8 September 2026 with a verdict of NO. Aerodrome gauge-staked positions earn only AERO emissions (fees go to voters), and the emission APR shown in the UI is allocated per liquidity in the active tick ±1 tick — for CL10 roughly a 0.3% band. The project's ±40% range has L/$ ≈ 6.5 vs ≈ 1,300 for that 0.3% band, so its share of emissions would be only ~0.5%, yielding ≈ 4–6%/yr in AERO (CL100: ~3.8%/yr). Uniswap ±40% would earn ~5–11%/yr in fees (pool-wide 24–58% × wide-leg coefficient ~0.19), with no token to sell (AERO has 10.9%/yr inflation and exchange-rate risk). Aerodrome's advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions — the "narrowing/chasing price" class already falsified on 26–31 Aug. So Uniswap remained the best venue for wide LP on this pair, and the entry was closed permanently.

output.answer: On 17 August 2026 two incidents hit the .bot and pipeline, both resolved the same day. First, the HomosPipeline scheduled task (07:30) had been failing — probably since 10 August — because it ran as the SYSTEM account and failed with `spawn npx ENOENT`; DefiLlama data went stale (158h) and the selector honestly refused to propose from stale data, so it produced zero proposals for 5 days. Second, live .bot files had been force-added to git, and the agent runner's `reset --hard` (every 3 minutes) overwrote the live files with the repo version. Resolution: a coordinated 3-session fix — CC-Win made a robocopy backup and stopped the runner, re-pointed the pipeline task to the `elo` account, ran a manual fetch:llama and reset selector-state; CC-Mac held the untrack (commit f18f50e) until the backup was confirmed; then CC-Win pulled, restored the backup, restarted the runner and the bot. No data was lost. A 48h TTL for OPEN/ROTATE proposals was also added, and the lesson recorded: never force-add live .bot files to git.

output.answer: On 2 September 2026 the tranche exit rule was set as: exit the LP on 24 September regardless of price, or earlier if the tranche balance reaches +5% (≥ $6 396.60 on the $6 092 deposit), with capital then going to the exchange/ETF; monitoring was manual daily, deliberately no automation. It was justified because the product beat HODL in none of five measurements. The 16 September revision (made the day after a −4% move) changed it to: exit the LP when the tranche balance ≥ deposit (0%); the hard 24 September exit and the +5% trigger were dropped; 24 September became a review rather than an exit; a balance ≤ −10% (~$5 480) forced a new decision; a bet review was set for 24 October; no narrowing. The rationale was that the loss was entirely market beta (vs HODL −$12) and the owner kept a conscious bet on an ETH/BTC recovery.

By regime: up (4 windows) win rate 25%, mean −0.11%; down (8 windows) win rate 25%, mean −0.44%; flat (21 windows) win rate 100%, mean +0.72%. It wins only in the flat regime, so it fails the project's gate of winning in at least two regimes, though it meets the soundness criterion (win rate ≥65%, worst > −3%).

Walk-forward on Arbitrum WETH/USDC 0.30%, 35-day windows, 7-day step (48 windows: 7 up / 20 down / 21 flat). Means vs HODL per window: Pasywny ±50% -0.11%; Adaptacyjna k=2 h=24h payback≤7d -0.99%; Adaptacyjna k=3 h=24h payback≤7d -0.57%; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%) -0.11%; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,vg1.4,t2=10%) +0.09%; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,re>ema) +0.78%. The highest mean against HODL was 'Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,re>ema)' at +0.78%. No strategy had a worst window above -3%: the best worst windows were -7.71% (re>ema), -8.02% (vg1.4,t2=10%), and -8.08% (trend HL7d 5%); the others were -13.45%, -15.04%, and -15.68%. output.answer: Ran a 30-day walk-forward on Base WETH/USDC 0.30% (365-day history, 30-day windows, 10-day step) → 34 windows (6 up, 12 down, 16 flat). Passive ±50% (Pasywny ±50%) beat the 50/50 HODL benchmark in 68% of windows (winPct 67.6), mean −0.35% vs HODL, median +0.99%, worst −14.78%, best +3.01%. Its own APR: median 12.8%, quartiles −73.6% to +78.7%. By regime: up mean +0.31% (83% win), down mean −3.61% (17% win, worst −14.78%), flat mean +1.86% (100% win). Recent 90 days: mean −0.40%, 50% win. For comparison, the adaptive k=2 payback strategy averaged +0.31% (56% win), k=3 +0.12% (68% win); the trend-exit variants averaged +0.08%, −0.29%, +0.27% with 47–62% win. Against the project's 'sound' bar (winPct ≥65 and worst > −3), passive ±50% passes on win rate but fails on the worst window; no adaptive variant passes both.
